full_judgment:
2. The predecessor of respondents 1 to 6 Mahbubur Rahman @ Mujibur Rahman instituted Title Suit No. 12 of 1961 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Faridpur, for declaration of title to the suit lands described in Schedules Ka, Kha, Ga, Gha and Uma to the plaint and for confirmation of possession therein. The plaintiff's alternative prayer was for recovery of khas possession if they were found to have been dispossessed during the pendency of the suit. Plaintiff's case is that the suit land belonged to one Abdul Majid and his co-sharers (including the plaintiff himself in some of the suit lands) The plaintiff purchased the same from the heirs of Abdul Majid and others by registered Kabala dated 14th Bhadra, 1366 B.S. and he is in possession of the same for more than 12 years on payment of rent to the land-lords. Defendants were trying to disturb the possession of the plaintiff claiming that defendant nos. 1, 10 and Aminuddin predecessor of Defendants 2 to 9 took lease of the lands in Schedules Ka, Kha and Ga and that defendant nos. 12 and Mozammel predecessors of defend-ants 13 to 19 took lease of the Gha Schedule lands and further that defendant no. 11 and Aminuddin Sharif took lease of Uma Schedule lands from the landlords. The plaintiff instituted Miscellaneous Case No.137 of 1960 against the defendants under section 145 Cr.P.C. but the learned Magistrate, in that case, found possession of the lands with the defendants. 

 3. Plaintiff's further case was that the landlords were never in khas possession of the suit lands, that they never settled the same with the defendants and that the defendants had no manner of title to the suit lands, and being emboldened by the decision of 145 Cr.P.C. case, they threatened to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land on 7-7-60. Hence the suit. 

 4. The suit was contested by defendants 1, 2, 10, 12 and 14 by filing a joint written statement. They denied all the allegations made in the plaint and their case, inter alia, was that the Ka schedule lands were the khas lands of the landlords; that the interests of the original owners in respect of other Schedule lands were auction sold in execution of certificate cases for arrears of rent and the landlords auction purchased the same and after possessing the lands for some years, leased out the lands to the defendants, who are in possession of the same since their lease, that the plaintiff obtained Kabala without any consideration, from the heirs of the original tenants taking advantage of the wrong entry in the R.S. Khatians and the plaintiff acquired no title by virtue of the Kabala which was for no consideration. 

 6. The learned Subordinate Judge on retrial dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs and held that though the R.S. Khatians recorded the names of the plaintiffs and their predecessors the presumption arising out of the record of rights had been rebutted by the defendants by adducing evidence. He found the dakhilas filed by the plaintiffs to have been manufactured after the criminal proceeding under section 145 Cr.P.C. He also found that the suit lands were auction purchased by the landlords and that they entered into khas possession of the same after taking delivery of possession and being in possession they settled the schedule lands in favour of the defendants. He found that the Kabuliyats executed by the defendants were acted upon and that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit lands.
